chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام delivered a sermon on Eid al-Adha and said:

"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no deity but Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, and to Him belongs gratitude for what He has bestowed upon us. And all praise belongs to Allah for what He has provided us from the cattle of the grazing livestock."

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allah is the Greatest; the formula of takbir
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise and thanks belonging to Allah
key_terms.بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ: the sacrificial livestock from the cattle animals
key_terms.عِيدِ الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no deity but Allah; affirmation of tawhid

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali عليه السلام say in his Eid al-Adha sermon about takbir and gratitude to Allah?
ai.summary: This report preserves a proclamation delivered by Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام on Eid al-Adha. It centers on takbir, praise, and gratitude to Allah for guidance and for providing the sacrificial animals associated with this sacred occasion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1483 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) delivered a sermon on Eid al-Adha, saying:

"Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest. There is no deity but Allah (swt). Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, and all praise belongs to Allah (swt). Allah (swt) is the Greatest for guiding us, and to Him belongs gratitude for what He has granted us. All praise belongs to Allah (swt) for what He has provided us from the sacrificial animals."
